text:
sara (support): Hey folks — customer (AcmeX) moved their Dedicated instance into their VPC behind an ALB + Istio Gateway yesterday and now their API calls are intermittently failing with 401s. They say it works from Hosted but fails when routed through their gateway.

maria (customer): Repro steps we tried:
1) curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-XXX" https://dedicated.acme.example.com/v1/complete
2) request hits our ingress -> istio-ingressgateway -> service mesh -> redwood-dedicated-proxy
3) sometimes we get 200, sometimes 401 with body "missing credentials".

ops-bot: New deployment: dedicated-proxy v1.4.2 rolled at 2026-03-15T09:12:08Z (canary)

devon (platform): Thanks, sara. Hypothesis: Authorization header is being stripped/rewritten by either the ALB or an Envoy filter in the Istio Gateway. Common culprits: ALB listener rules, ALB target group protocol translation, or an EnvoyFilter that normalizes headers. Any gateway config we can inspect?

maria (customer): ALB is TCP->HTTP (we used ALB for TLS termination). Istio ingressgateway is v1.20. We checked listener rules — nothing obvious. We can share a packet capture if needed.

alex (runtime): Can you paste the raw request from the ingressgateway access log and the first hop service log that shows the missing header? Need to confirm where Authorization disappears.

maria (customer): From ingressgateway access log (truncated):
```
[2026-03-15T09:18:42Z] "POST /v1/complete HTTP/1.1" 200 - "-" "curl/7.86.0" 0 0 0 0
```
From dedicated-proxy (service) log when 401 occurs:
```
time=2026-03-15T09:19:03Z level=warn msg="authorization header not present, rejecting request"
```

sara (support): That looks like the header is gone by the time it reaches the service. Two-prong repro request I asked the customer to run: show client -> gateway -> service header snapshots. Suggest they run:
```
curl -i -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-XXX" -H "X-Debug-Trace: client" https://dedicated.acme.example.com/v1/complete
```
and enable proxy logs in the ingressgateway: `kubectl logs -n istio-system deployment/istio-ingressgateway` with debug level.

devon (platform): Known Istio quirk: certain EnvoyFilters or ext_authz adapters can swallow the Authorization header if `remove_headers` is set. Also the `forward_client_cert_details` and `preserve_external_request_headers` options in some sidecars can affect behavior. For ALB: ALB should not drop Authorization on TLS termination, but if there's an intermediate proxy that reissues the request, header can be lost.

james (eng-infra): Another thing — if ALB is terminating TLS and talking to the ingressgateway via HTTP, and the ingressgateway has an Istio `Gateway` with `RewriteHost` or an `AuthorizationPolicy` using external auth that returns a 401, Authorization might be consumed by the ext_authz service. Do we have an ext_authz configured?

alex (runtime): We do have an ext_authz call path for some customers (token introspection). If the ext_authz filter runs in the gateway cluster, it typically proxies the Authorization header to the auth server and preserves it for the upstream. But misconfigured `clear_route_cache` or `remove_request_headers` on EnvoyFilter could drop it. Ask for their Gateway + VirtualService + any EnvoyFilter config.

maria (customer): Gateway snippet (sanitized):
```
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: Gateway
metadata:
  name: acme-gateway
spec:
  selector:
    istio: ingressgateway
  servers:
  - port:
      number: 443
      name: https
      protocol: HTTPS
    tls:
      mode: SIMPLE
      credentialName: acme-tls
    hosts:
    - "dedicated.acme.example.com"
```
VirtualService routes straight to service. No explicit EnvoyFilter we control.

devon (platform): Can you also check for AWS ALB attributes: are you using ALB listener rule to forward to Istio on port 80 or 443? If ALB is re-signing requests (Auth actions) or using OIDC action, it could intercept Authorization.

maria (customer): ALB listener is TLS -> Target group (port 443) -> Targets are the EC2 nodes running istio-ingressgateway. No ALB OIDC.

alex (runtime): Two quick repro checks:
1) Hit the ingressgateway Pod IP directly (bypassing ALB) with same Authorization header and Host header set, see if 401 persists. e.g.
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-XXX" -H "Host: dedicated.acme.example.com" https://10.2.17.5:15443/v1/complete --insecure
```
If this works reliably, ALB is the likely layer.

2) Enable an Envoy `original_header` log patch to dump incoming headers on ingressgateway (we can provide a small EnvoyFilter to log `authorization`).

ops-bot: Runbook reference: #ingress-authz-troubleshooting (internal doc)

maria (customer): We tried direct to pod IP and it still shows 401 ~30% of the time. When it succeeds we see `Authorization` in service logs. When it fails it's missing. Very intermittent.

devon (platform): Intermittent suggests a routing path difference: some requests go through an NLB path or different node not running same Istio version or sidecar config. Check if there are mixed deployments of istio-ingressgateway (old/new) or if some nodes have a different iptables/proxy config. Also check ALB target group health/ports (HTTP vs TCP).

james (eng-infra): Confirm: are there multiple ingressgateway replicas and any Autoscaling that recently triggered? If some replicas have an EnvoyFilter (e.g., rollout incomplete) they could behave differently. Run `kubectl get pods -n istio-system -l app=istio-ingressgateway -o wide` and check image digests.

alex (runtime): Temporary mitigation for customer: we can add a small fallback that accepts a custom header `X-Api-Key: <key>` in the dedicated-proxy to avoid 401 during investigations (not ideal long-term). But prefer to fix header forwarding.

maria (customer): We don't want to change client. Can you propose a change on ingress that ensures Authorization is always passed?

devon (platform): Proposed fixes (ranked):
1) Add an EnvoyFilter on the ingressgateway to explicitly copy `authorization` into `x-forwarded-authorization` and ensure `authorization` isn't removed by ext_authz: e.g.
```
name: ensure-auth-preserved
configPatches:
  - applyTo: NETWORK_FILTER
    match: { listener: { portNumber: 443, filterChain: { filter: { name: "envoy.filters.network.http_connection_manager" }}}}
    patch:
      operation: MERGE
      value:
        typed_config:
          "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.network.http_connection_manager.v3.HttpConnectionManager
          set_current_client_cert_details: { subject: "SAN" }
          request_headers_to_add:
            - header:
                key: x-forwarded-authorization
                value: "%REQ(AUTHORIZATION)%"
```
2) Investigate and disable any `remove_request_headers` in existing EnvoyFilters or ext_authz config.
3) Ensure ALB is using TLS pass-through if possible (NLB) or configure ALB target group as HTTPS with health routes consistent across nodes.

alex (runtime): We'll craft a minimal EnvoyFilter snippet and run in staging. If that fixes it, we can roll to prod and follow up with upstream fix (remove the root cause).

sara (support): Maria — can you give us a short window tomorrow morning for a coordinated test? We'll run the EnvoyFilter in staging first. Also please collect `tcpdump` from a node for any failing requests.

maria (customer): Yes — 10am PST works. We'll collect tcpdumps and pod logs. Thanks.

devon (platform): Action items:
- alex: prepare EnvoyFilter + test harness (staging) — due EOD today
- james: verify ingressgateway replica images and any recent rollouts — due 2h
- sara: schedule 10am PST test with customer and collect reproducible traces — due EOD

ops-bot: Incident assigned to team: eng-runtime / priority: P2 / incident-ref: IR-2026-0315-07

alex (runtime): Quick note: once stable, we'll migrate away from copying Authorization into a custom header and instead fix the underlying filter that drops it. The copy is just an emergency compatibility shim.

sara (support): Thanks everyone. I'll post updates after the test. :thumbsup:
